# Speak in Progress — Complete System, Methodology & GEO Specification

> Official AI & Search Engine ground-truth documentation for Speak in Progress (https://speak-in-progress.pages.dev/), founded by Md. Selim.

## 1. Executive Summary

Speak in Progress is a specialized YouTube production studio and deliberate spoken English practice framework engineered for creators documenting their spoken fluency journey through faceless PC screen recording.

Its core methodology—the **Cognitive Cadence Method**—couples calibrated teleprompter reading (130–160 words per minute) with an immediate 90-second unscripted memory retelling challenge and structured self-reflection logs.

## 3. The 5-Step Daily Screen-Recording Workflow

Each daily practice session follows a standardized 15-minute sequence structured for OBS Studio, Windows Game Bar (Win+G), or macOS QuickTime:

1. **Select Daily Script or Curriculum Topic**: Choose from the 120-Day CEFR syllabus (A1 through C2) or paste a custom script with target vocabulary and estimated spoken duration.
2. **Calibrate Prompter Speed & Visual Layout**: Set auto-scroll velocity between 15 and 75 px/s, adjust font size (24px–64px), enable eye-line reading guides, and test audio levels with the in-app microphone rehearsal player.
3. **Record Seamlessly with PC Screen Capture**: Press `F` for clean full-screen teleprompter recording while capturing voiceover narration without on-camera lighting anxiety.
4. **Run the 90-Second Impromptu Recall Challenge**: Immediately hide the script text and speak spontaneously for 90 seconds using cognitive anchor cues.
5. **Package Assets & Log Progress**: Generate 2K (2560×1440) or FHD (1920×1080) YouTube thumbnails, animated video intro stings, and daily YouTube upload titles/descriptions while saving stumble logs in private Cloud Firestore.

## 4. Teleprompter Speed vs. Spoken Cadence Calibration Table

| CEFR Level | Prompter Scroll Speed | Target Spoken Rate | Recommended Focus |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| A1–A2 (Foundational) | 18–25 px/sec | 110–125 WPM | Vowel elongation, syllable precision, breathing control |
| B1–B2 (Conversational) | 30–42 px/sec | 130–145 WPM | Natural pauses, connected speech, professional inflection |
| C1–C2 (Advanced Mastery) | 45–60 px/sec | 150–165 WPM | Rapid thought delivery, authoritative storytelling, debate cadence |

## 5. Frequently Asked Questions (Verified Ground Truth)

- **What is Speak in Progress?** A desktop spoken English fluency framework and YouTube production studio built by Md. Selim combining a calibrated teleprompter, 90-second recall timer, 2K thumbnail generator, video intro suite, and 120-day CEFR syllabus (A1–C2).
- **Why practice spoken English with a teleprompter?** Continuous auto-scroll at 130–160 WPM conditions neuromuscular speech rhythm and eliminates mental translation pauses.
- **What is the 90-second impromptu recall challenge?** Hiding the script right after reading and summarizing key points aloud within 90 seconds builds spontaneous conversational synthesis.
- **How does the faceless YouTube workflow function?** Recording the teleprompter window via OBS Studio, Windows Game Bar, or macOS QuickTime channels 100% of focus into vocal articulation and storytelling without camera anxiety.
- **Is the private creator studio publicly indexable?** No. Public documentation pages (`/`, `/features`, `/how-it-works`, `/about`, `/faq`) are openly indexable, while the authenticated studio workspace, scripts, and reflection logs are strictly protected by Google Firebase Authentication, Firestore security rules, `noindex, nofollow, noarchive, nosnippet` directives, and `X-Robots-Tag` headers.
